## How the SOFAR Channel Carries Whale Calls Across the Ocean

The SOFAR channel is a naturally occurring pathway in the ocean through which low-frequency sound can travel long distances. Sound waves bend up and down through the channel, allowing a hydrophone positioned near its axis to detect sounds from far away, including whale calls.

In some instances, low-frequency sound can travel across entire ocean basins. This reach helps explain how hydrophones can detect distant whale calls.
